title.zh: 终态分子压力与温度归约

summary: Reduce a terminal H2 distribution to centered pressure and temperature profiles using a caller-supplied thermal speed, mass ratio and cylindrical velocity quadrature.

identity.relation: terminal H2 pressure and temperature reduction
identity.direction: terminal (vr,vx,x) distribution, velocity nodes, explicit mass and thermal speed, quadrature -> two x profiles
identity.definition: For each spatial cell k, density=sum_i weight[i]*sum_j f[i,j,k]*dvx[j] and flux=Vth*sum_i weight[i]*sum_j vx[j]*f[i,j,k]*dvx[j], with the stated per-cell matrix-vector and radial reduction order. The centered squared normalized speed is vr[i]^2+(vx[j]-flux/(density*Vth))^2. Pressure is 2*mass_ratio*1.6726231e-27*Vth^2/(3*1.602177e-19) times its weighted distribution integral; temperature is pressure/density. Density must be strictly positive in each spatial cell, but individual weights may be zero.
identity.model: terminal H2 centered-moment diagnostic with caller-supplied mass ratio and thermal speed
identity.geometry: one-dimensional x profile over cylindrical (vr,vx) velocity cells
identity.coordinates: vr and vx are dimensionless speeds normalized by the supplied thermal speed; vr is nonnegative and vx may be signed
identity.boundary: finite nonnegative nonempty three-dimensional distribution; finite one-dimensional aligned velocity nodes and nonnegative quadrature weights; positive scalar mass ratio and thermal speed; positive integrated density in every x cell
assumptions: On positive quadrature weights this pressure and temperature relation agrees with the corresponding fields of scirel.kinetic.axisymmetric-neutral-moments when that asset's derived thermal speed equals this caller-supplied speed and molecularity is 2. This relation allows zero weights and computes no stress or heat flux.
The mass ratio multiplies the frozen hydrogen mass constant, not a standard atomic mass unit; the H2 pressure uses twice that mass.

The callable neither establishes the incoming terminal distribution nor validates the full terminal closure. Boolean, complex and numeric-string coercions are excluded by the maintained real-numeric contract.

inputs.name: vr
inputs.constraints: Finite, nonnegative, nonempty and one-dimensional; zero nodes are allowed and no monotonicity gate is imposed.

inputs.name: vx
inputs.constraints: Finite, nonempty and one-dimensional; zero nodes are allowed and no monotonicity gate is imposed.

inputs.name: mass_ratio
inputs.description: Positive factor of the frozen hydrogen mass used for the H2 particle mass.
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive; boolean and numeric-string coercions are rejected.

inputs.name: thermal_speed_m_s
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive; no speed is derived from temperature in this callable.

inputs.name: terminal_distribution
inputs.description: Terminal H2 velocity distribution by spatial cell.
inputs.constraints: Finite, nonnegative and nonempty with exactly three axes.

inputs.name: cylindrical_weight
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative; zero cells are allowed if every integrated density remains positive.

inputs.name: dvx
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative; zero cells are allowed if every integrated density remains positive.

outputs.name: pressure_profile_ev_m3
outputs.units: eV/m^3 on the source distribution normalization

outputs.name: temperature_profile_ev
outputs.description: Pressure divided by integrated number density.
outputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative; density is strictly positive.

preconditions: The caller supplies a terminal H2 distribution aligned to the explicit cylindrical velocity quadrature.
Each spatial slice has strictly positive integrated density.
supported: Stateless terminal H2 pressure and temperature reduction on finite cylindrical carriers, including some zero quadrature cells.
excluded: Higher stress and heat moments, terminal generation-state selection, wall-source feedback and external physical validation.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for non-real numeric or non-finite inputs, malformed axes, negative radial nodes/distribution/weights/widths, nonpositive mass ratio or thermal speed, or nonpositive integrated density.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError if integrated density, pressure or temperature becomes non-finite, or if a computed pressure or temperature is negative; no partial mapping is returned.

python.signature: reduce_terminal_molecular_pressure_temperature(vr, vx, mass_ratio, thermal_speed_m_s, terminal_distribution, cylindrical_weight, dvx)

example.description: Reduce one terminal H2 spatial cell with a zero axial node and a zero-width cell.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.kinetic import reduce_terminal_molecular_pressure_temperature
vr = np.array([0.5, 1.0])
vx = np.array([-1.0, 0.0, 2.0])
f = np.ones((2, 3, 1))
r = reduce_terminal_molecular_pressure_temperature(vr, vx, 1.0, 5000.0, f, np.array([1.0, 2.0]), np.array([0.5, 0.0, 0.25]))
assert set(r) == {'pressure_profile_ev_m3', 'temperature_profile_ev'}
assert r['pressure_profile_ev_m3'].shape == (1,)
assert all(np.isfinite(value).all() for value in r.values())
example.expected: Two finite one-cell profiles; a zero axial node and a zero-width cell are accepted when integrated density remains positive.

scope: Independent centered per-cell second-moment reduction checks both outputs on a nonuniform signed carrier.
Positive-weight overlap agrees with the existing nine-moment relation; zero-weight acceptance distinguishes their contracts.
Three digest-pinned fixed cases cover exact finite agreement and the boolean-coercion divergence.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Direct numerical comparisons establish the finite discrete centered-moment relation and boundary differences on tested carriers. They do not establish the incoming terminal distribution, physical normalization, complete qualification or expert approval.
known_limitations: Numerical agreement with the reference cases is bounded evidence and does not establish full qualification.
The physical normalization of the supplied distribution requires expert review.
